ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The ethylene precursor substance ACC can generate ethylene under the action of oxidase ACO, while acetyltransferase B (NatB) will promote the acetylation of ACO, thereby affecting the degradation rate of ACO. It is known that ethylene content is related to the bending angle of the tip of Arabidopsis seedlings. To explore the mechanism by which NatB regulates plant ethylene synthesis, researchers carried out related experiments, and the results are shown in the figure. Question: Can exogenous application of ACC increase or decrease the bending angle of the tip of NatB mutant plants?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the vertical axis is the bending angle of the tip of Arabidopsis seedlings, with the unit being degrees; the legend shows that the white bars are air treatment, and the black bars are ethylene treatment. Under air treatment, the bending angle of the tip of NatB mutant plants is about 110°; under ethylene treatment, the bending angle of the tip of NatB mutant plants rises to about 160°. This indicates that in NatB mutant plants, enhanced ethylene action will increase the bending angle of the seedling tip. Then reason: The question stem states that ACC is an ethylene precursor and can generate ethylene under the action of ACO, so exogenous application of ACC will increase ethylene synthesis or ethylene level. Since ethylene treatment in the figure increases the bending angle of the tip of NatB mutant plants, exogenous application of ACC should also increase the bending angle of the tip of NatB mutant plants.
